title: How to start using evolving rep ranges in your training
summary: NH explains how to phase evolving rep ranges into a program gradually: start with reps only on isolation lifts, then upper body compounds, then lower rep ranges on compounds, and finally lower body lifts with one set at a time. Full adoption took him 1.5-2 years and full understanding about three.
claims: Treat any new method like a new lift or diet: give yourself an adaptation period
Don't replace all rep ranges with evolving ones at once: they're hard to track, throw off tonnage and can stall progression
When starting, vary only the reps and keep sets static; reps usually trigger set changes and two moving variables is too much
Many lifters already use an evolving range like 4x8-12 on isolation moves; that 'hypertrophy rep range' doesn't really exist
Don't carry an 8-12 range from isolations onto deadlift or squat variations; it's a recipe for disaster
Step 1: switch all isolation exercises to evolving ranges; small muscles give quick feedback and the risk is low
Step 2: move evolving ranges to upper body compounds, which carry less tonnage than squats or deadlifts
Separate upper and lower body lifts by quality so half the program can be evolving while the other stays static
Most people's upper body lacks volume: too much horizontal pressing, neglected curls, triceps, wrist curls and vertical press
Low evolving ranges (3x3-5, 5-7) belong mostly on compounds like bench and overhead press
Small muscle groups should mostly get higher reps because their joints and structures are fragile; very experienced lifters can carefully do 3-5 on biceps
Before higher evolving reps on squats and deadlifts, build stamina with back-off sets at 65-70%, once a week or every two weeks
Static rep ranges camouflage poor cardiovascular stamina; a 6-10 on stiff-leg deadlifts will expose it
Replace the back-off set with one evolving set on a single movement pattern; never squats and deadlifts together, and never several evolving lower body patterns in one day
Three or four extra reps barely matter on 50 lb triceps extensions but add a lot of tonnage on a 200 lb squat
Evolving ranges trickle down toward failure every set (8, 7, 6, 5 reps), so the muscle gets very fatigued
Spread evolving ranges like a drop of ink rather than dumping the inkwell on the page
The end goal is mostly evolving ranges with a few static ones for steady tonnage; the last phase is high-intensity low-rep evolving ranges on lower body lifts
Evolving rep ranges help avoid plateaus and accumulate high-quality tonnage
NH took 1.5-2 years to convert his whole program to evolving ranges and about three years to understand how they interact
Write your training down to learn from your body as ranges evolve
